plan: Queue carry as primary. It is Cuban's best role at 56.8% over 191 games (overall is 51.5%). Set offlane as secondary, not the other way around.
Stop queueing midlane: 46.0% over 237 games is costing real VP. When auto-filled there, play the safest comfort pick, not a learning pick.
Two-hero rule for the climb: Sparrow and Serath. Compared with the average player on the same hero, Cuban wins about 3.6 and 3.0 more games per 100 on them.
Cuban's champion pool is 13+ heroes wide and the top three are only 32% of the games. Gold-to-Platinum climbs are almost always pool-narrowing stories: aim for 70%+ of games on the top three.
The math: Cuban is at 500 VP; Platinum III starts at 900. The all-time peak is 824.
honesty: personal winrates are shrunk toward the player's own average (small heater samples do not count as mains)
field baselines are all-ranks aggregates from our current-patch match sample, not Gold-bracket-specific yet
winrate edges are observational; they say where the player wins, not why

insights.title: Goldilocks324 brings out Cuban's best
insights.finding: Cuban's record alongside Goldilocks324 is 57% over 269 ranked games — the strongest pairing in the stack. When only two of the squad queue, make it this pair.

insights.title: For the group chat
insights.finding: 2 pentakills in real 5v5s and a longest spree of 21 (plus 27 more in ARAM and brawls — the group chat can rule on whether those count). Cuban has receipts.

insights.title: Cuban's lean, relative to the squad: objective damage
insights.finding: Cuban's profile sits mid-pack on most axes; the clearest lean is objective damage at 1.1x the squad average. Steady is a style too — the lineup can build around predictability.

insights.title: Cuban punches back after losses
insights.finding: Cuban wins MORE right after a loss (55%) than after a win (30%). Tilt is not the problem; complacency might be.
insights.receipt: 6/11 after losses vs 3/10 after wins, last 22 games
